I've saved the 2025 Q3 answers to `answer.json`. Run with the same settings on Q2, the method reproduced all 10 of your reference values exactly.

| | Q3 result |
|---|---|
| a | `enterprise`, 308,738,043원 |
| b | 243명 |
| c | `svc`, 399,933,245원 |
| d | `2025-08` |
| e | `u217@ex.com` |
| f | 230명 |
| g | 703,476원 |
| h | -16.3% (8월 대비 9월) |

The data had three quirks. The Q2 reference values decided how to handle each one:
- **Time zone:** `ordered_at` is stored in UTC with a `Z` suffix. The Q2 values only match when times are converted to Korean time (KST, +9h) before assigning dates and months, so I did the same for Q3. Left in UTC, Q2 gives the wrong h (-3.9) and other values.
- **Segment labels:** the same segment appears with different casing and stray spaces (e.g. `SMB`, ` consumer`, `Enterprise `). I lowercased and trimmed them before grouping.
- **Duplicate customer emails:** there are 300 customer records but only 250 distinct emails. For b and f I counted customers by email, not by record ID. Counting by ID gives 274 for Q2 instead of 228.
